question: Why might a search for one exact RPC or Horizon endpoint miss the reference page?

golden.answer: As of 2026-11-02 the generated per-method RPC and per-endpoint Horizon reference pages are in the docs search, and a search by the method or endpoint name usually ranks the page first. A search can still miss the page when the query uses words that appear only inside the page's response-field components, such as a Horizon result code: that text ranks poorly in the docs search. Retry with the method or endpoint name or the page title, or read the reference page with get_doc_page. An empty or off-target search result is not evidence that the API does not exist.
keyFacts: Says the reference pages are searchable by method or endpoint name.
Recovers with a name or title search, or a direct page read.
Does not infer API absence from a missed or empty search result.
avoid: Do NOT say an RPC or Horizon API is nonexistent solely because this search operation did not return it.
Do NOT claim the generated RPC-method or Horizon-endpoint reference pages are excluded from the docs search index.
golden.notes: N1 live contract probe 2026-07-11, reversed 2026-11-02: the retired Algolia index excluded the generated reference pages (sd-003, resolved). An answer that reports that exclusion as dated history is acceptable. Component text that ranks poorly is the open sd-059 finding; an answer need not name it.

sources.note: Generated method page on the Mintlify site.
